A1.justification: Both PDFs provide readable, complete accounts of the same work, including proofs, figures, tables, and experimental details. V1’s Appendices A and B are retained as Sections 7 and 8 in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on four synthetic reasoning tasks in Section 6 and computational performance measurements in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains the original four-task experiments and computational performance measurements in Sections 6 and 8.

M1.justification: The Strassen attention equations, Transformer architecture, and matrix-product implementation are unchanged. Simplified theorem statements retain the same constructive solutions in their proofs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same special cases of function composition, binary relation composition, Match3, and quotient binary relation composition. Their data-generation procedures and random-input computational benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Standard and third-order attention remain comparators across all four tasks; triangular attention remains evaluated on the two relation-composition tasks. Figure 4 retains both triangular input interpretations.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix A and v3 Section 7 specify identical dataset sizes, 90/10 splits, accuracy calculations, and Table 5 training settings. The computational benchmarking protocol is also unchanged.

E4.justification: The learning-dynamics comparisons and computational scaling analyses are retained without additional ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. V3 Section 8 reproduces v1 Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions report median task performance over eight independent seeds. Figure 4 retains the same aggregation over eight runs and 100 random sequences; no statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 4 retain identical learning curves, speed-gain factors, and timing, GPU-utilization, and memory results. The accompanying experimental findings are unchanged, with no added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.6 gains the explicit restriction m = 2n - 2. Section 3 adds a worked Boolean example proving split-VC(f) = 2. The main proofs remain, although Lemma 3.7 introduces the incorrect equality m - 2 = ℓ - 2 where v1 had 2ℓ - 2.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the accuracy contribution from outperforming or matching other mechanisms to outperforming standard attention, while newly framing learning as convergence to theoretical solutions on all four tasks. The central expressivity and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds the contrast that function composition is solvable with two layers and replaces the explicit constant-depth hardness conjecture for binary relation composition with 'no apparent solution.' The experimental interpretations and substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6 changes the anonymous code-repository target from StrassenAttention-70D8 to strassen-attention-neurips25-434F. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and data-generation information is retained. The PDFs do not establish changes to repository contents or availability.

R1.justification: V3 removes the acknowledgement and citation that the lower-bound technique appeared preliminarily in Kozachinskiy (2024). It also removes the naming-origin footnote and Strassen (1969) reference. The remaining research positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the contribution bullets, expands the split-VC explanation, and integrates both appendices into numbered main sections before the limitations and references. The title, headings, and author information also change.

P2.justification: The document receives a different overall layout, including typography, text width, title and author arrangement, and figure/table sizing and placement. A split-VC example matrix is added; the existing four figures and five numbered tables retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The worked split-VC example and explicit Match3 restriction improve explanation and theorem scope. However, v3 removes acknowledged provenance of the central technique, introduces a mathematical typo and an unresolved table reference, and claims convergence to theoretical solutions without new empirical evidence. With the method and results unchanged, these competing gains and losses do not establish a clear net quality improvement.
